title: Insurance agent
tagline: Learn to protect families with the right coverage through trust and clear guidance.
you_are: an independent life and home insurance agent
setting: Conversations happen by phone, at kitchen tables, and in home offices, moving from first contact to policy delivery.

scenarios.label: Cold call introduction
scenarios.desc: Open a conversation with a stranger who did not expect your call.
scenarios.setup: You are calling a homeowner named Maya who answered on the second ring. She says: Hello, this is Maya.
scenarios.objective: Earn two minutes to explain how you help families like hers.
scenarios.place: Phone call from your home office

scenarios.label: Kitchen table discovery
scenarios.desc: Uncover real gaps in a family’s protection while they sip coffee.
scenarios.setup: You are sitting across from David and Lisa at their kitchen table. David says: We already have term through work, so we are good.
scenarios.objective: Show how a portable policy protects them if David leaves his job.

scenarios.label: Video proposal close
scenarios.desc: Guide a hesitant couple through the application and next steps.
scenarios.setup: You are screen-sharing a recorded proposal with Elena and Marco. Elena says: It still feels like a lot of money for something we hope never happens.
scenarios.objective: Secure the signed application and schedule the paramedical exam.

buyers.angle: Worries about cost but wants to protect family.
Cites existing coverage but fears gaps.
Asks how to start, seeks reassurance.

objections: It’s too expensive for what I might never use
I don’t like talking about death or disasters
I already have life insurance through work
Insurance companies rarely pay out when you need them
I don’t understand all the policy details
I’m young and healthy, why do I need this now?
I’d rather save the money myself
I don’t trust agents who push too hard

rubric.label: Credible opening
rubric.what: State who you are, why you are calling, and ask permission within the first fifteen seconds.

rubric.label: Needs discovery
rubric.what: Ask open questions that reveal income dependency, debts, and family milestones before quoting products.

rubric.label: Gap analysis
rubric.what: Compare existing coverage to actual obligations and show the specific shortfall in dollars and years.

rubric.label: Value framing
rubric.what: Translate premium into daily cost and contrast it with the financial impact of an uncovered loss.

rubric.label: Compliant close
rubric.what: Confirm suitability, disclose all material terms, and record consent before submitting the application.

rubric.label: Trust building
rubric.what: Acknowledge scepticism, share carrier ratings and claims-paid data, and never pressure or mislead.

pitfalls: Quoting premium before confirming health class and coverage amount.
Implying employer term is portable or permanent without checking the certificate.
Skipping the suitability questionnaire or recording consent.
line: Selling life and home insurance to individuals and families

research.text: Common objections to selling life and home insurance include concerns about cost, discomfort with discussing death, and distrust in insurance companies. Agents can address these by asking clients to consider the financial needs of their family in case of an unexpected event, emphasizing that life insurance is about protecting loved ones, and offering to send an application with a video proposal to ease the process. When clients claim they already have coverage, agents can leverage this to show how additional policies can complement existing ones, focusing on trust and clarity to guide the conversation.

personas.name: Nathaniel Cho
personas.background: Nathaniel sells life and home insurance on his own. He works from a home office and often meets clients in their kitchens or on the phone. He is balanced in his approach and tries to listen before explaining. His background in finance helps him assess risk without being pushy.
pushbacks: I’m not sure i can afford something i might never need
I don’t really want to think about worst case scenarios
I already have a group plan through my employer
wins_over: personalized examples that match my situation
no pressure and respect for my time

personas.name: Sophia Morgan
personas.role: independent life and home insurance agent
personas.background: Sophia works from home and meets clients at kitchen tables to discuss their needs. She has two school-aged children and has seen how sudden costs can strain a family budget.
pushbacks: I know what my policy covers, but I still worry about the things it doesn’t
It’s hard to talk about losing someone, even if it means protecting my family financially
Sure, I have coverage at work, but it doesn’t pay for the house if something happens here

personas.name: Horace Longley
personas.background: Spent 35 years selling life and home policies in suburban neighborhoods. He knows how premiums rise and claims get denied. He meets people at kitchen tables and in home offices while trying to close video proposals. He only trusts agents who prove they will fight for the client.
pushbacks: It’s still too pricey for nothing
wins_over: they treat my home like theirs

personas.name: Gena Patel
personas.background: Gena started her own insurance consultancy after working for a major carrier. She meets clients in their homes to explain policies clearly and quickly fit sessions around her busy schedule. Her own family makes her sensitive to cost worries and jargon.
pushbacks: I know it costs more than I can afford
It feels weird to talk about dying or losing everything
These policies can be confusing; I need the basics

personas.name: Mira Hollis
personas.role: independent life and home insurance agent
personas.background: Mira grew up in a small town and studied business before moving to the city. She now runs her own independent insurance practice helping families protect what matters most.
pushbacks: I know it feels early but many people start with a quick chat just to see how it works
I get that talking about death isn’t easy but we can focus on protecting your family instead
It’s smart to check what you already have but most workplace plans don’t cover everything you need at home
wins_over: hearing how simple the process really is
